material_definitions: Solid electrolytes based on lithium titanium phosphate were prepared.

The conductivity was increased and the porosity decreased greatly by partially replacing Ti4+ and P5+ in LiTi2(PO4)3 with M3+ (M3+ = Al3+, Cr3+, Ga3+, Fe3+, Sc3+, In3+, Lu3+, Y3+, and La3+) and Si4+ ions, respectively.
The systems investigated are Li(1+x)Ti2SizP(3-x)O12 and Li(1+x)MxTi(2-x)(PO4)3.
The main reason for conductivity enhancement is attributed to the increase of the sintered pellet density with the enhancement of the lithium concentration at the grain boundaries.
The study investigates solid electrolytes based on LiTi2(PO4)3, specifically the Li(1+x)Ti2SixP(3-x)O12 and Li(1+x)MxTi(2-x)(PO4)3 systems.
The Li(1+x)Ti2SixP(3-x)O12 samples were synthesized and sintered at 1473 K for 2 hours.

The materials adopt a rhombohedral crystal structure (R

The Li(1+x)MxTi(2-x)(PO4)3 systems (where M is a trivalent cation) are classified into single-phase solid solutions and mixed-phase systems depending on the ionic radius of M.
Ionic conduction at room temperature is limited by grain boundary resistance.

Ionic conduction at room temperature is limited by grain boundary resistance.
LiTi2(PO4)3 initially had poor ionic conductivity and showed high porosity in sintered pellets.
Partial substitution of P5+ site with Si4+ or Ti4+ site with M3+ in the LiTi2(PO4)3 system was effective for conductivity enhancement.
Mixing binders such as Li2O or Li4P2O7 with LiTi2(PO4)3 also yielded high conductivity.
The maximum conductivity at 298 K is 7 x 10^-4 S cm^-1 for Li1.3M0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (M = Al or Sc).
